blocks.task_summary: Find the 13th term of an arithmetic sequence given the 1st term 36 and 5th term 12.
method_path: Find common difference d using u5 = u1 + 4d
accepted_alternatives: Use u13 = u5 + 8d after finding d

evidence.basis: attempt to find the common difference (M1); 12 = 36 + 4d OR (12-36)/(5-1); d = -6 (A1); attempt to use the term formula (M1); u13 = u1 + 12(-6) OR u5 + 8(-6); u13 = -36 A1

blocks.task_summary: Find n such that the sum of the first n terms of the arithmetic sequence is zero.
accepted_alternatives: Recognize symmetry: terms sum to zero when positive and negative terms cancel, giving n=13

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: attempt to set Sn = 0 (M1); n/2 [2(36) + (n-1)(-6)] = 0 OR n/2 (36 + un) = 0 => un = -36; n = 13 A1. METHOD 2: attempt to recognize symmetry (M1); 36+30+...+0+...-30-36; n = 13 A1.

accepted_alternatives: Factorize and cancel in one step: (x(x-1)(x+1))/((x-7)(x-1)(x+1)) = x/(x-7)
Rewrite as (x(x^2-1))/((x-7)(x-1)(x+1)) and cancel

evidence.basis: attempt to factorize at least one expression (M1); correct factorization and cancellation leading to x/(x-7) (A1)

method_path: Use log property: log_2 A - log_2 B = log_2(A/B)
Use result from part (a) to simplify left side to log_2(x/(x-7))
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2: Rewrite 1 as log_2 2, use quotient rule to get log_2[(x(x^2-1))/2] = log_2[(x^2-8x+7)(x+1)], then equate arguments and simplify to x/(x-7) = 2, giving x = 14

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: attempt to use subtraction/quotient property of logs (M1); valid attempt to rewrite equation with or without logs (M1); x/(x-7) = 2 (A1); x = 14 (A1)

blocks.task_summary: Find the value of c and a for the parabola y = ax^2 + c passing through P(0,9) and Q(3,0).
method_path: Write down c = 9 from point P(0,9).
Substitute Q(3,0) into y = ax^2 + c with c = 9.

blocks.task_summary: Find the area of the region enclosed by the line y = -3x + 9 and the parabola y = -x^2 + 9.
method_path: Set up integral of (parabola - line) from x=0 to x=3: ∫[0,3] ((-x^2+9) - (-3x+9)) dx = ∫[0,3] (-x^2+3x) dx.
Subtract value at 0 (0) to get area = 9/2.
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2: Evaluate ∫[0,3] (-x^2+9) dx and subtract triangle area (1/2*3*9) or evaluate ∫[0,3] (-3x+9) dx separately and subtract.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: attempt to subtract areas (M1); ∫[0,3] (-x^2+3x) dx; correct integration (A1); attempt to substitute limits (M1); Area = 9/2 A1. METHOD 2: correct integration (A1); substitute limits (M1); subtract integrals (M1); Area = 9/2 A1.

blocks.task_summary: Show that p = -1 given that the vertex A of f(x) = -x^2 + 4x + p lies on the line y = 2x - 1.
method_path: Find x-coordinate of vertex A: x = -b/(2a) = -4/(2*(-1)) = 2
Substitute x = 2 into line equation y = 2x - 1 to get y = 3
Substitute x = 2 into f(x) = -x^2 + 4x + p, set equal to 3, solve for p: -4 + 8 + p = 3 => p = -1
accepted_alternatives: Find x-coordinate of vertex A = 2, substitute into f(x) to get f(2) = p + 4, set equal to 2(2)-1 = 3, solve p = -1.
Complete the square: f(x) = -(x-2)^2 + 4 + p, vertex A(2, 4+p), substitute into line: 4+p = 2(2)-1 => p = -1.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: x-coordinate of the vertex at A is 2 (A1); attempt to substitute their x-coordinate into equation of line (M1); 2(2)-1=3; 3 = -2^2 + 4(2) + p; p = -1 AG. METHOD 2: x-coordinate of the vertex at A is 2 (A1); attempt to substitute their x-coordinate into f(x) (M1); f(2) = p+4; p+4 = 2(2)-1; p = -1 AG. METHOD 3: attempt to complete the square on f(x) (M1); -(x-2)^2 + 4 + p; A x=2 OR A y=4+p (A1); 4+p = 2(2)-1; p = -1 AG.

blocks.task_summary: Find the value of q given that the vertex B of g(x) = x^2 + qx - 1 lies on the line y = 2x - 1.
method_path: Find x-coordinate of vertex B: x = -q/2
Substitute x = -q/2 into line equation y = 2x - 1 to get y = -q - 1
Substitute x = -q/2 into g(x) = x^2 + qx - 1, set equal to -q - 1, simplify to q^2 - 4q = 0
Solve quadratic: q(q - 4) = 0, discard q = 0 (non-zero constant), so q = 4
accepted_alternatives: Find x-coordinate of vertex B = -q/2, substitute into g(x) to get y = -q^2/4 - 1, set equal to 2(-q/2)-1 = -q-1, solve q^2 - 4q = 0, q = 4.
Complete the square: g(x) = (x + q/2)^2 - q^2/4 - 1, vertex B(-q/2, -q^2/4 - 1), substitute into line: -q^2/4 - 1 = 2(-q/2) - 1 => q^2 - 4q = 0, q = 4.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: x-coordinate is -q/2 (A1); attempt to find intersection points, equating g(x) and 2x-1 (M1); x^2 + qx - 1 = 2x - 1; attempt to substitute their x-coordinate (M1); (-q/2)^2 + q(-q/2) - 1 = 2(-q/2) - 1; q^2 - 4q = 0 (A1); q = 4 (since q ≠ 0) A1. METHOD 2: x-coordinate is -q/2 (A1); EITHER attempt to substitute their x-coordinate into y=2x-1 (M1); 2(-q/2)-1 => B(-q/2, -q-1); attempt to substitute their coordinates of B into g(x) (M1); -q-1 = (-q/2)^2 + q(-q/2) - 1; OR attempt to substitute their x-coordinate into g(x) (M1); (-q/2)^2 + q(-q/2) - 1 => B(-q/2, -q^2/4 - 1); attempt to substitute their coordinates of B into the line (M1); -q^2/4 - 1 = 2(-q/2) - 1; THEN q^2 - 4q = 0 (A1); q = 4 (since q ≠ 0) A1. METHOD 3: attempt to complete the square on g(x) (M1); (x + q/2)^2 - q^2/4 - 1; B x = -q/2 OR y = -q^2/4 - 1 (A1); attempt to substitute their coordinates of B into equation of line (M1); -q^2/4 - 1 = 2(-q/2) - 1; q^2 - 4q = 0 (A1); q = 4 (since q ≠ 0) A1.

blocks.task_summary: Find α and β for which the linear system has infinitely many solutions.
method_path: Set third row coefficients to zero for consistency
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2: Eliminate one variable, substitute into third equation, set coefficients to zero.
METHOD 3: Add/subtract equations, compare coefficients with third equation.
METHOD 4: Vector approach: find direction vector of intersection of first two planes, require normal of third plane perpendicular to it, then find β using a common point.
METHOD 5: Find general point on line of intersection of first two planes, substitute into third plane, require coefficient of parameter zero and constant term equal to β.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1 Row Reduction: attempt to reduce a matrix or eliminate one variable (M1); two correct rows or equivalent equations A1A1; correct third row or equivalent equation A1; equating the third row coefficients to zero (M1); α = 2 and β = 10 A1.

METHOD 2 Writing an equation in one variable: attempt to eliminate either x or z using the first two equations (M1); one correct equation A1; correct substitution into the third equation to create an equation in either x or z A2; attempt to set coefficients equal to zero for infinite solutions (M1); α = 2 and β = 10 A1.
METHOD 3 Subtracting and comparing equations: attempt to add or subtract two equations (M1); A2; attempt to compare coefficients with the third equation (M1); α = 2 and β = 10 A1A1.

METHOD 4 Vector approach: attempt to find direction vector of line of intersection using π1 and π2 (M1); d = (2, -3, 2) A1; normal of π3 is perpendicular to d (M1); α = 2 A1; correct substitution of a point common to the first two planes into the third plane A1; β = 10 A1.

METHOD 5 Finding a general point on the line of intersection: attempt to find intersection of π1 and π2 (M1); x = 4 + 2t, y = 3 - 3t, z = 2t A1A1; correct substitution of general point into π3 A1; recognizing that the coefficient of t must be zero OR the constant term must be β (M1); α = 2 and β = 10 A1.

blocks.task_summary: Show that sin 3θ ≡ 3 sin θ − 4 sin³ θ.
method_path: Express sin 3θ as sin(2θ + θ) using angle sum formula
Apply double angle identities for sin 2θ and cos 2θ
Use Pythagorean identity to express cos² θ in terms of sin θ
Simplify to 3 sin θ − 4 sin³ θ
accepted_alternatives: Use de Moivre's theorem: (cos θ + i sin θ)³ = cos 3θ + i sin 3θ, expand LHS, equate imaginary parts, and simplify using cos² θ = 1 − sin² θ.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: attempt to use angle sum formula (M1), sin 2θ cos θ + cos 2θ sin θ (A1), attempt to use a double angle identity or the Pythagorean identity (M1), 2 sin θ cos² θ + (1 − 2 sin² θ) sin θ OR 2 sin θ (1 − sin² θ) + cos 2θ sin θ, leading to 3 sin θ − 4 sin³ θ (A1). METHOD 2: (cos θ + i sin θ)³ = cos 3θ + i sin 3θ (A1), attempt to expand LHS (M1), comparing imaginary parts (M1), sin 3θ = 3 cos² θ sin θ − sin³ θ (A1), then 3 sin θ − 4 sin³ θ.
